title: Agent Technology Radar — Source Registry
description: Schema for config/default-sources.json (the source registry), version 2. IMPORTANT: unrelated to config/config-schema.json, which describes the end-user config at ~/.follow-builders/config.json. Entries are validated at runtime only for a subset (see loadSources in scripts/generate-feed.js), but this file is the written specification.
$comment: v2 flattens the registry: v1's three container arrays (podcasts/blogs/x_accounts) encoded channel in the container itself, which does not extend to rss/github/api/etc. Now channel is explicit data.

schemaVersion.description: Structure version of the registry. v1 = three arrays (podcasts/blogs/x_accounts); v2 = flat sources[].

sourceId.description: Stable identity, format `<channel>:<slug>`. Hand-assigned and stored literally — NEVER derived at runtime from `name` or a URL, so renaming a display name or changing a URL cannot silently change identity. Immutable once published: Phase 2's signal `source_id` refers back to this value. The prefix encodes the CHANNEL (not the role), so role can change without breaking identity.

role.description: WHY this source is worth tracking — a Radar-semantics question, orthogonal to how it is fetched. Frozen at these five values for v1; adding one requires explicit justification. `official` = vendor/institution first-party; `builder` = practitioners who ship; `researcher` = people doing research; `community` = third-party open-source projects; `aggregator` = a discovery surface whose content is NOT first-hand.

channel.description: HOW the content is fetched — an engineering question that determines which fetcher runs. Only x / blog / podcast currently have a fetcher; every other value requires new code, so such entries must stay active:false.

tier.description: Human-assigned attention classification — how much attention the source deserves. NOT a score, NOT a weight, and not an input to any computation. Weighting is a Phase 3 concern.

name.description: Display name. Not an identity — changing it must not change `id`.

active.description: true = eligible for fetching; false = registered but skipped by the loader. Entries whose channel has no fetcher yet MUST be false.

url.description: YouTube channel/playlist URL used for title-matching an episode's exact video URL. Read by fetchPodcastContent.

indexUrl.description: Read by fetchBlogContent. The parser is dispatched by SUBSTRING MATCH on this value (generate-feed.js:912-916: `anthropic.com` / `claude.com`), and the article extractor likewise by the article URL (:961-965). A blog on a new domain therefore still needs a code change.

type.description: CONFIRMED UNUSED — zero code references. Cleanup deferred to a later phase.

articleBaseUrl.description: CONFIRMED UNUSED — zero code references. Article URLs are hardcoded instead (generate-feed.js:686, 709, 734). Cleanup deferred.

fetchMethod.description: CONFIRMED UNUSED — zero code references. Cleanup deferred.

handle.description: X handle WITHOUT a leading @. Read by fetchXContent, which resolves the numeric user id at runtime — it is deliberately not stored.

rssUrl.description: Generic RSS/Atom feed. Needs a fetcher that does not exist yet.

repo.description: `owner/name`. Signal = releases. Needs a fetcher (keyless, unauthenticated rate limit 60 req/h). Release noise (nightly/preview tags) will need filtering.

endpoint.description: Full URL to query. Needs a fetcher per channel.

url.description: Page to scrape. Needs a generic web fetcher.
